key_insight: Long-range variational circuits are fragile when fault phases interfere destructively with target-energy performance, not simply when faults spread widely.
engineering_relevance: Ansatz design should balance expressivity and gate-count exposure while controlling transverse catalysts that activate otherwise energetically dark faults.
method: Prove contrasting energy damage for equally extensive faults in Heisenberg chains.
Compare noisy training with nonuniform rotations and pair-flip gate components suppressed separately or together.
Predict noise-induced energy shifts using single-fault fragility and gate-count exposure λ = pK.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an exact N/2 energy-damage ratio for equally extensive faults, halved dephasing error when both catalysts are suppressed, and rescue of every tested trapped trajectory by annealing transverse catalysts.
watch_item: The reported mechanisms concern Heisenberg chains and specified circuit and noise settings; broader hardware and Hamiltonian generalization needs validation.
paper_title: Phase Interference and Transverse Catalysts Govern the Noise Fragility of Long-Range Variational Quantum Circuits
